page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by a 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC 9T34 processor. Built on KVM virtualization, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, along with 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is paired with 16.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It includes no local storage or discrete GPUs, relying on remote cloud storage and cloud networking with a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded CPU capability. The instance achieved a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 3115.38 (top 10%) and a Geekbench single-core score of 2005.0 (top 25%). Supported instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (Foundation, VNNI, BF16) and cryptographic accelerators (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). Multi-threaded compute throughput sits in the middle tier, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 12465.68 and a PassMark CPU score of 14617.84 across its 8 threads.

Memory bandwidth tests show 47.95 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 28.19 GB/sec for writes, placing RAM throughput in the middle performance tier. Application benchmarks demonstrate stable performance across web and caching tiers, reaching 11.16 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.4 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The 1:2 memory configuration provides efficient dedicated compute for instruction-heavy tasks without allocating redundant RAM overhead. Primary hardware trade-offs include the lack of bundled local NVMe storage and absence of hardware accelerators. As a result, ecs.c8ae.2xlarge is well positioned for compile clusters, CI/CD runners, batch computational processing, web application serving, and microservices.
